issues.display_title: Issue #486: Stop Missing-Row Requeue Loops in Banned Workers
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Stop Missing-Row Requeue Loops in Banned Workers

Changes

  • Updated BannedComment, BannedPost, and BannedUser workers under one task.
  • Added per-worker settlement helpers using errors.Is(err, gorm.ErrRecordNotFound).
  • Missing required rows now call delivery.Ack(false) and log skip missing row.
  • Other processing failures still call delivery.Reject(true) for retry.
  • Invalid JSON and invalid payload handling remain Reject(false).
  • Added focused settlement regression tests for all three workers.

Tests

  • Confirmed TDD RED before each helper existed: focused packages failed with undefined: settleBanned*Failure.
  • Added tests covering missing-row acknowledgement and generic-error requeue behavior.

Verification

go test -count=1 ./src/Worker/...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All worker packages pass.
  • All three banned-worker regression test packages pass.
  • Whitespace validation passes; Git only reports line-ending warnings.

Problem

BannedComment, BannedPost, and BannedUser reject every processing error with requeue enabled. When a referenced post, comment, moderated user, or reporter has been deleted, GORM returns gorm.ErrRecordNotFound. RabbitMQ then repeatedly delivers the same stale message and may repeat partial side effects.

Scope

  • Update all three banned workers in one task.
  • Acknowledge and skip gorm.ErrRecordNotFound messages.
  • Keep requeue enabled for other processing failures.
  • Log missing-row skips.
  • Add regression tests for each worker.
  • Preserve queue names, payloads, validation, status processing, and normal success acknowledgements.

Acceptance Criteria

  • All three workers acknowledge missing-row failures without requeueing.
  • Other processing failures continue to requeue.
  • Invalid JSON and invalid payloads continue to reject without requeue.
  • Focused worker tests pass.

Delivery

  • Implemented locally.
  • Not committed or pushed.

issues.display_title: Issue #487: Fix init post active and pending defaults
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Initialize Post Active and Pending Defaults

Changes

  • Updated newInitPost to assign non-nil boolean pointers explicitly:
    • Active = true.
    • Pending = false.
  • Kept the existing post ID, slug, publish, processing, uploading, and response behavior unchanged.
  • Added a focused regression test for both values.

Because InitAddPost passes the returned model directly to Config.DB.Create, the non-nil pointers make GORM include both columns in the insert instead of writing NULL.

Tests

  • Added src/Action/V1/Posts/InitAddPost_test.go.
  • Confirmed TDD RED before implementation: active must default to true.
  • Verified Active is non-nil and true.
  • Verified Pending is non-nil and false.

Verification

go test ./src/Action/V1/Posts -count=1

Result: post package tests pass. Independent review found no issues.

Problem

POST /post/init creates a GORM Models.Post with Active and Pending left as nil pointers. GORM inserts SQL NULL, so database defaults (active = true, pending = false) are not applied.

Scope

  • Set active = true explicitly in newInitPost.
  • Set pending = false explicitly in the same flow.
  • Preserve current ID, slug, publish, processing, uploading, and response behavior.
  • Do not change schema, backfill existing rows, or alter other post creation flows.
  • Add a focused regression test.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Posts created through /post/init store active = true.
  • Posts created through /post/init store pending = false.
  • Neither field is inserted as NULL.
  • Existing rows remain unchanged.
  • Focused post package tests pass.

Delivery

  • Implemented in commit 2923c92d.
  • No additional commit or push performed.
